author: Adam Kinunen
text: He is a fool who turns exceptions into rules.
note: Relative-universal formula. No published source found for the wording; the formula itself is ancient.

ancestors.text: He is a fool who envies the happiness of the proud.
They make a rule of exception... But of the exception you make a rule without exception.
Youths and women want the exceptions, old people the rules.
Every man, in his own opinion, forms an exception to the ordinary rules of morality.

author: Adam Kinunen
text: You are not allowed to disparage the power of your vacuum until after you have cleaned the filter.
note: Deontic prohibition with a maintenance precondition - a rule of standing, not a moral rule. Modern domestic image in the Twain/Wilde register. No published source found.

ancestors.text: Great difference between a good Tool and a good Workman.
A bad workman blames his tools.

author: Adam Kinunen
text: Exceptions may only explode absolute rules; the bar is much higher, more difficult and less wise to dissolve a general rule, which by its very nature admits exceptions.
note: A canon about rule-types rather than a maxim about conduct. States in one sentence the distinction Holton draws between simple universal generalisations (which admit only counterexamples) and defeasible rules (which admit exceptions without rejection). Marked draft: see open question in the spec.

ancestors.text: exceptio probat regulam in casibus non exceptis - the exception proves the rule in cases not excepted.

ancestors.cite: Richard Holton, 'The Exception Proves the Rule'
ancestors.text: Distinguishes simple universal generalisations, which admit only counterexamples, from defeasible rules, to which exceptions can be made without rejecting the rule.
They make a rule of exception...
